subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The time T of one complete oscillation of a simple pendulum of length l is given by T = 2π√(l/g), where g is the gravitational constant. Find the approximate percentage error in T when the percentage error in l is 1%.

mark_split.label: Write T as a constant times √l
Divide by T and put 1% in

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what is constant in the formula, and what the square root does to the percentage error.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write T as a constant times √l
steps.margin_note: First mark. Separate what varies from what does not. Only l is measured here, so 2π and g go into one constant before anything is differentiated.
steps.memory_tip: Only l is measured. Put 2π and g into a single constant k and differentiate √l alone.
lines: Here 2π and g are constants, so put k = 2π/√g.

recall.must_convey: That 2π and g are constants, so T = k√l with k = 2π/√g, and this is differentiated with respect to l.
accept: two pi and g are constants so T is a constant times root l
put k equals two pi by root g and differentiate root l
only l changes, everything else is constant
g constant, so T equals k into root l ani raasi differentiate cheyyali
separate the constant part from the square root of l

steps.why: The error is made in l only; g is a constant and contributes no error. Writing T = k√l says that on the page and reduces the whole question to differentiating a square root.
common_mistakes: Treating g as a variable and differentiating it as well.
Differentiating √(l/g) as 1/(2√(l/g)) and losing the 1/√g factor.

steps.label: Divide by T and put 1% in
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The constant k cancels in the ratio, so the answer does not depend on g at all. The square root halves the percentage error.
steps.memory_tip: A square root is the power ½, so it halves the percentage error: half of 1% is 0.5%.
lines: Percentage error in T = (1/2) × percentage error in l

lines.text: ∴ the approximate percentage error in T is 0.5%

recall.must_convey: That dT/T = ½(dl/l), so a 1% error in l gives a 0.5% error in T.
accept: d T over T is half of d l over l so the answer is zero point five percent
the square root halves it, half of one percent
percentage error in T is half a percent
root undi kabatti sagam, zero point five percent
one half into one percent is zero point five percent

steps.why: √l is l to the power ½, and for a power law the relative error is multiplied by the exponent. The exponent here is ½, so the percentage error is halved. That the constant k cancels is the check that g never enters the answer.
common_mistakes: Giving 1% by carrying the error across unchanged.
Giving 2% by multiplying by 2 instead of by ½.

insider_note: T depends on √l, so the index is 1/2 and the relative error is HALVED, not doubled. The constants 2π and g cancel out of dT/T entirely.
